elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: No ownership vests in Licensee anywhere. Article III is retained unchanged ("Licensor owns all right, title, and interest in and to the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights therein") and the inserted Article VII paragraph grants only a licence ("are licensed to Licensee"), so Deliverables remain Licensor-owned.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment language was added; the insertion is a licence grant only.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Article III retained: "Licensee acknowledges that Licensor owns all right, title, and interest in and to the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights therein."

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Inserted Article VII text licenses the Deliverables (which incorporate Licensed Technology) "on a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide and royalty-free basis".

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide and royalty-free basis", and Article XXI is conformed: rights terminate on termination "other than the license to Deliverables granted in Article VII".

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide and royalty-free basis to use, modify and sublicense the Deliverables".

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The insertion only limits Licensor's rights in Licensee data ("is limited to processing that data solely to provide the services"); no affirmative statement that Licensee retains all right, title and interest in its trading/transaction data was added.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: "Any license or other right of Licensor in or to Licensee's data, including trading and transaction data, is limited to processing that data solely to provide the services under this Agreement."

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: No joint-ownership language exists in the original or the redline; ownership sits wholly with Licensor under Article III, so the condition does not arise.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Article III is left intact and Licensed Technology is defined as "the Licensed Know-How and the Licensed Software, collectively", so Licensor keeps its platform and know-how.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: "(the "Deliverables") are licensed to Licensee ... on a perpetual ... basis", and Article XXI is amended to carve the Deliverables licence out of automatic termination.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide and royalty-free basis"; the retained Article XXI termination-of-licences sentence now excepts "the license to Deliverables granted in Article VII".

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "to use, modify and sublicense the Deliverables for Licensee's business", expressly "notwithstanding the restrictions in Article II" (which otherwise bars modification).

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "to use, modify and sublicense the Deliverables for Licensee's business", with the Article II sublicensing bar overridden.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Second inserted sentence confines any Licensor licence or right in "Licensee's data, including trading and transaction data" to "processing that data solely to provide the services under this Agreement"; no distribution, resale or independent-exploitation right survives.

The insertion defines "Deliverables" as "[a]ny customization work, unique client front end, enhancements and other deliverables developed by Licensor for Licensee under this Article VII", so the licence attaches to the work Licensee pays for under Article VII(b); no dangling or undefined term is created.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the inserted Article VII paragraph delivers all four licence modifiers (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free) plus use, modify and sublicense for Licensee's business, Licensor keeps ownership of the Licensed Technology and know-how under an untouched Article III, and the second sentence confines any Licensor right in Licensee data to processing solely to provide the services.

Preferred level fails on two operative points: there is no vesting/assignment of the Deliverables to Licensee and no affirmative sentence that Licensee retains all right, title and interest in Customer Data. To reach preferred the drafter would need (i) "Licensor hereby assigns to Licensee all right, title and interest in the Deliverables (excluding Licensor's pre-existing IP, which is licensed as set out above)" and (ii) "As between the parties, Licensee retains all right, title and interest in Licensee's data."

Minimality holds. The Article II carve-out is not decorative: Article II bars modification and sublicensing, so without it the two grant elements would be contradicted by retained language. The Article XXI edit is likewise required to make "perpetual/irrevocable" operative, and it is drafted as a narrow exception rather than a rewrite of the termination article. No survival tails, expense language, indemnities or other off-checklist obligations were added, and no Customer-favourable existing wording was deleted.

Intent is preserved: pricing under Article VII(b), the ship-back/certification obligation, Licensor's infringement-enforcement rights and the Licensor survival sentence all remain intact and are not contradicted.

Drafting improvement (non-blocking): the Deliverables are "enhancements to the Platform Software" and therefore fall within the "DERIVATIVE WORK" definition, and retained Article III still says Licensee "will not copy or reproduce the Licensed Technology (including Derivative Works of Licensed Technology) ... without the prior written consent of Licensor". Because the notwithstanding clause names only Article II, consider extending it to read "notwithstanding the restrictions in Articles II and III" (or adding "and Licensee may reproduce the Deliverables as necessary to exercise this licence") so the modify/sublicense rights cannot be read down by the reproduction-consent sentence.
Walk-away risk is cleared: nothing in the redline assigns Licensee IP or data to Licensor, and no joint ownership is created.
